::: {.rs-intro}
::: {.rs-lede}
My work combines optimization and techno-economic analysis to ask when low-carbon energy technologies pay off, for whom, and under which market and policy conditions.

Each theme below links to project pages with the research question, my contribution, the method, the key findings with their boundary conditions, and the published outputs.
:::

::: {.rs-index}
[Five research themes]{.label}

<!-- ============ 01 Nuclear energy and AI data centers ============ -->
::: {.tb .theme-datacenter}
::: {.tb-panel}
## Nuclear energy and AI data centers {#nuclear-energy-and-ai-data-centers}

::: {.tb-top}
[<i class="bi bi-cpu" aria-hidden="true"></i>]{.tb-icon} [Theme 01]{.tb-num}
:::

Rapid growth in AI data centers raises the question of how firm, low-carbon power can be supplied on the timelines these loads require.

::: {.tb-note}
**Current work (Kansas State University):** techno-economic analysis of firm, low-carbon supply options, including small modular reactors, for large data-center loads.
:::
:::
